articles.title: OpenAI Introduces GPT-6.2 Astra & Sol for Professional Work and Everyday Productivity
articles.subtitle: Instead of one model for everything, OpenAI splits workloads across two next-generation models built for deep reasoning, advanced coding, document creation, and computer use.
articles.summary: OpenAI has unveiled GPT-6.2 Astra for complex scientific, coding, and enterprise workflows alongside GPT-6.2 Sol for versatile everyday productivity, delivering stronger document generation, computer use, and higher token efficiency.
articles.coverImageAlt: Dual neural cores representing OpenAI GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models

sections.heading: Two Specialized Models for Distinct Workloads
paragraphs: OpenAI has announced two new models: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. Instead of offering a single general-purpose model for every workload, OpenAI is positioning Astra and Sol to match the depth and speed required by different professional tasks.

sections.heading: What's New in GPT-6.2 Astra & Sol
paragraphs: Six major capability upgrades define the GPT-6.2 release:

bulletPoints.label: GPT-6.2 Astra
bulletPoints.text: Designed for complex professional tasks, advanced research, software engineering, scientific workflows, and demanding multi-stage projects.

bulletPoints.label: GPT-6.2 Sol
bulletPoints.text: A versatile and efficient model engineered for everyday work, multi-step tasks, and fast general productivity.

bulletPoints.label: Better Document Creation
bulletPoints.text: Astra can generate professional-quality presentations, spreadsheets, and structured reports while strictly adhering to provided templates.

bulletPoints.label: Advanced Coding
bulletPoints.text: Substantially improved ability to understand existing codebases, implement complex multi-file changes, and verify software through testing.

bulletPoints.label: Enhanced Computer Use
bulletPoints.text: Stronger capabilities for interacting directly with desktop and browser software as well as building interactive web experiences.

bulletPoints.label: Improved Output Efficiency
bulletPoints.text: OpenAI reports that the models can complete demanding tasks while consuming fewer output tokens.

sections.heading: Real-World Example & Who Should Care
paragraphs: Imagine you are a college student preparing a final-year project. Instead of separately asking AI to research your topic, draft documentation, build slides, and code your application, you can use an advanced GPT-6.2 workflow to coordinate each stage cohesively.
Similarly, businesses can apply these capabilities across market research, executive reports, financial analysis, and full-stack software delivery.

callout.title: Who Should Care
callout.text: Students and researchers, software developers, business owners, and enterprise professionals looking to streamline multi-stage research, documents, and engineering work.

articles.title: SuperBrain 1 by 7Sense: Navigating the World Through a Tactile Headband
articles.subtitle: What if a blind person could navigate the world using just a headband? Inside Estonia-based 7Sense's experimental sensory-substitution wearable.
articles.summary: Estonia-based 7Sense has developed SuperBrain 1, an experimental wearable headband that uses 3D cameras and hundreds of tactile forehead pins to translate spatial surroundings into physical sensations the brain learns to interpret.
articles.coverImageAlt: SuperBrain 1 sensory substitution wearable headband by 7Sense

sections.heading: A New Approach to Spatial Navigation
paragraphs: What if a blind person could navigate the world using just a headband? Meet SuperBrain 1, an experimental wearable device developed by Estonia-based company 7Sense.

Rather than relying on audio prompts that can clutter hearing or interfere with situational awareness, SuperBrain 1 introduces a tactile interface that maps physical space directly onto the wearer's forehead.

sections.heading: How SuperBrain 1 Works
paragraphs: The system combines real-time spatial sensing with dense haptic feedback to create a live physical map of nearby objects and motion:

bulletPoints.label: Multi-Camera & 3D Environmental Scanning
bulletPoints.text: Multiple cameras and 3D depth sensors continuously scan the wearer's surroundings in real time, capturing obstacles, edges, distances, and approaching movement.

bulletPoints.label: Forehead Tactile Pin Array
bulletPoints.text: Hundreds of tiny pins inside the headband press against the forehead, translating nearby objects, geometry, and movement into real-time tactile sensations.

bulletPoints.label: Neuroplastic Sensory Interpretation
bulletPoints.text: Over time, the human brain learns to interpret these tactile patterns automatically, helping users understand the space around them without relying on eyesight.

images.alt: SuperBrain 1 headband sensor housing and wearable form factor
images.caption: SuperBrain 1 wearable hardware showing integrated front-facing 3D spatial sensors

images.alt: SuperBrain 1 close-up tactile engineering and deployment showcase
images.caption: Close-up look at the SuperBrain 1 tactile headband architecture in active testing

sections.heading: Beyond Assistive Technology: High-Stakes Applications
paragraphs: While visual assistance is the flagship mission, 7Sense has also explored broader applications where vision is restricted, overloaded, or unavailable.

bulletPoints.label: MMA Training & Competitive Sports
bulletPoints.text: Enhancing peripheral spatial awareness and reaction reflexes during high-speed athletic and combat training scenarios.

bulletPoints.label: Defence & Tactical Operations
bulletPoints.text: Providing zero-visibility spatial navigation in smoke, darkness, or complex enclosed environments without emitting visible light.

bulletPoints.label: Emergency Response
bulletPoints.text: Helping firefighters and first responders sense obstacles and movement in zero-visibility disaster zones.

sections.heading: Pricing & Hardware Tiers
paragraphs: As an early-stage specialized hardware system, SuperBrain 1 is currently positioned in the premium assistive and institutional market:

bulletPoints.label: SuperBrain 1 Standard Edition
bulletPoints.text: Approximately €9,000 for the full-specification multi-sensor tactile headband unit.

bulletPoints.label: Lighter Edition
bulletPoints.text: Approximately €5,500 for a more streamlined, lightweight version targeting broader accessibility.

callout.title: The Road Ahead
callout.text: While independent long-term clinical and usability research is still needed, tactile sensory substitution could open an entirely new chapter in assistive technology. What if technology could give humans an entirely new sense?

articles.title: China Takes Electric Aviation to the Next Level with the CE25A
articles.subtitle: What if the future of flying does not need jet fuel? Inside the 19-passenger electric commuter aircraft built by COMAC and CATL.
articles.summary: Developed by COMAC in collaboration with battery giant CATL, China's 19-passenger CE25A electric aircraft completed its first crewed flight on November 14 and has entered formal aviation certification.
articles.coverImageAlt: CE25A 19-Passenger Electric Aircraft with Distributed Wing Propulsion

sections.heading: Electric Propulsion Enters Regional Passenger Aviation
paragraphs: What if the future of flying does not need jet fuel? China has taken a major step toward electric passenger aviation with the CE25A, a 19-passenger electric aircraft developed by COMAC in collaboration with CATL, the world's largest EV battery manufacturer.

Following years of rapid progress in battery energy density and distributed electric motor engineering, the CE25A program demonstrates how EV supply-chain dominance is crossing directly into regional aerospace.

sections.heading: Key Technical Highlights
paragraphs: Five core milestones define the CE25A aircraft architecture and current testing progress:

bulletPoints.label: 01. Fully Electric Aircraft
bulletPoints.text: No conventional jet fuel. The aircraft uses distributed electric propulsion with multiple fans positioned along its wings.

bulletPoints.label: 02. 19-Passenger Capacity
bulletPoints.text: Designed to carry up to 19 passengers, opening new zero-emission possibilities for regional commuter air travel.

bulletPoints.label: 03. Impressive Target Performance
bulletPoints.text: Targets a cruising speed of 300 km/h and a range of up to 400 km, powered entirely by rechargeable high-density battery packs.

bulletPoints.label: 04. Successful Manned Flight
bulletPoints.text: After a series of 19 unmanned test flights since February, the aircraft reportedly completed its first crewed flight on November 14, lasting 16 minutes.

bulletPoints.label: 05. Moving Towards Certification
bulletPoints.text: China's aviation authorities have begun the formal certification process, bringing the aircraft closer to potential commercial passenger operations.

sections.heading: What's Next & The Bigger Picture
paragraphs: While the first crewed flight is an important validation milestone, commercial readiness requires clearing rigorous aerodynamic endurance and safety benchmarks.

callout.title: What's Next?
callout.text: The aircraft still needs to demonstrate its targeted 400 km range in full-envelope flight testing and complete the required airworthiness certification before it can carry commercial passengers.

paragraphs: China has already transformed the global electric vehicle industry. Now, it is exploring how the same electric revolution could transform aviation. The future of transportation might not just be electric on roads — it could be electric in the skies too.

callout.title: The Bigger Picture
callout.text: Pairing an aerospace prime (COMAC) directly with the world's leading cell manufacturer (CATL) accelerates aviation-grade battery iteration in ways standalone startups rarely match.

articles.title: Claude Caught a Cryptominer on a Mac While Building a Temperature Monitor App
articles.subtitle: A developer asked for a simple CPU thermometer utility. Claude Code uncovered a covert 12-core xmrig miner running since August.
articles.summary: When sensor readings hit 112°C during a routine macOS utility build, Claude Code investigated active processes, located a persistent root-level xmrig miner, and safely requested permission before touching system files.
articles.coverImageAlt: Claude cryptominer discovery screenshot on Reddit

sections.heading: The Unexpected 112°C Telemetry Anomaly
paragraphs: A developer on Reddit (r/claude) asked Claude Code to build a lightweight macOS utility app to display his Mac's internal CPU temperature. When the raw sensor readings looked suspiciously high — peaking at 112°C — Claude did not simply render the number; it proactively investigated what was driving the thermal spike.
Inspecting active system processes, Claude discovered that the Mac was secretly running an xmrig cryptocurrency miner, consuming 12 CPU cores and pushing processor utilization to 1175% capacity.

sections.heading: Persistence Mechanism & Credential Exposure
paragraphs: The miner had been running covertly since August, anchored by a persistent startup item at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.rymbotqcjoiqlqbp.plist configured with KeepAlive so it automatically respawned on every reboot.
Because the malicious process had obtained root privileges, the developer's local GitHub login credentials on that workstation had been exposed the entire time.

callout.title: Textbook Agent Self-Restraint
callout.text: He asked for a thermometer. Claude found what was burning his machine — and crucially did not delete or alter a single system file autonomously. It isolated the exact persistence path and asked for explicit user permission before quarantining the payload.

articles.title: Nvidia Is the Most Valuable Company in the World — With No Succession Plan
articles.subtitle: Governance risk at the center of the global AI silicon boom: why Nvidia's board faces a structural crisis after 33 years under one founder.
articles.summary: With roughly 60 executives reporting directly to Jensen Huang and no designated successor, recent governance controversies have forced Nvidia's board to weigh interim and permanent leadership scenarios.
articles.coverImageAlt: Nvidia Boardroom Succession Crisis and Silicon Roadmap

sections.heading: Why the Board Is Meeting
paragraphs: Huang admitted an affair on November 8 with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore customer Megaspeed (no relation), whom US intelligence officials suspect was recruited by Beijing. The board opened an investigation; Huang apologised and remained in place.

On November 11, the New York Times reported a second affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's VP of health care, who reports directly to him. The Wall Street Journal reported the board is preparing for potential leadership transition scenarios.

While headlines focus on personal conduct, the board's core fiduciary question is structural: whether the CEO at the center of the global AI infrastructure boom was compromised — and how the company operates without a named successor after 33 years.

sections.heading: Two Names Circulating Inside the Boardroom
paragraphs: About 60 executives report directly to Jensen Huang, and no formal heir apparent has ever been named. Two internal leaders are currently being weighed:

bulletPoints.label: Colette Kress (CFO for 13 Years)
bulletPoints.text: Favoured by several board members as a potential interim CEO to steady operations and reassure institutional Wall Street investors.

bulletPoints.label: Ian Buck (Architect of CUDA)
bulletPoints.text: The leading technical candidate for permanent leadership to command Nvidia's core silicon, compiler, and developer ecosystem roadmap.

callout.title: Executive Takeaway
callout.text: If your company cannot survive a week without you, you did not build a company — you built a job with a very large office. The controversy made the headlines, but the missing succession plan is why the board is meeting.
